hypotheses.text: Biallelic PLAA variants reported in fetal series with major extraneural structural anomalies (such as skeletal dysplasia or genitourinary defects) reflect either secondary dual diagnoses in consanguineous pregnancies or variants of uncertain significance, rather than genuine monogenic causality of extraneural organogenesis defects by PLAA.
hypotheses.rationale: While postnatal pediatric PLAA cohorts display exclusively central nervous system degeneration (progressive microcephaly, spastic tetraparesis, leukoencephalopathy) with complete sparing of extraneural organs, fetal exome cohorts ascertain deceased fetuses on ultrasound anomalies and identify PLAA variants alongside skeletal and genitourinary findings. Distinguishing true pleiotropy from ascertainment bias or dual recessive pathology is critical for prenatal and postnatal genetic counseling.

evidence.text: In a prenatal whole-exome sequencing study of 61 deceased fetuses with ultrasound abnormalities, compound heterozygous variants in PLAA were identified among the positive cases; ultrasound abnormalities across the cohort included skeletal system abnormalities in 39.2% (11/28), multiple system abnormalities in 17.9% (5/28), and genitourinary abnormalities in 17.9% (5/28).

evidence.text: Consanguineous populations show a 2.78% to 2.93% rate of dual or multiple distinct autosomal recessive diseases, demonstrating that co-occurring congenital structural anomalies in recessive neurodegenerative cohorts can arise from independent homozygous loci rather than single-gene pleiotropy.

hypotheses.text: Complete loss-of-function nullizygosity of PLAA produces an embryonic- or fetal-lethal phenotype featuring multi-organ dysplasia detectable on prenatal ultrasound, whereas hypomorphic missense or splicing variants permit fetal survival and manifest postnatally as an isolated neurodegenerative disorder.
hypotheses.rationale: In animal models and several essential endosomal sorting/autophagy machinery disorders, complete biallelic knockout disrupts universal cellular homeostasis and embryogenesis, whereas partial loss-of-function variants spare systemic embryogenesis but cause selective vulnerability in post-mitotic neurons.

evidence.text: Retrospective exome sequencing in deceased fetuses terminating gestation or suffering intrauterine demise with severe structural defects discovered pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in PLAA, suggesting that the most severe presentations of PLAA deficiency may culminate in fetal demise with multi-organ ultrasound abnormalities.

hypotheses.text: In postnatal surviving patients diagnosed with PLAA deficiency, the prevalence of major non-CNS congenital structural anomalies (including congenital heart disease, renal agenesis/dysplasia, and limb reduction defects) is less than 5%, confirming that their presence in a living infant with progressive microcephaly points to an alternative syndromic diagnosis.
hypotheses.rationale: Clinicians evaluating an infant with progressive microcephaly and spasticity need sharp rule-out criteria. If major extraneural structural malformations are essentially unobserved in liveborn PLAA patients, their detection strongly redirects diagnostic suspicion to multi-system syndromic ciliopathies, peroxisomal disorders, or complex chromosomal/monogenic syndromes.

evidence.text: Investigation of genetic causes in atypical cerebral palsy and neurodevelopmental delay identified pathogenic PLAA variants in living patients characterized by neurodevelopmental delay, spasticity, and progressive neurological impairment, without reported extraneural congenital heart or renal malformations.

new_directions.question_text: In deceased fetuses with PLAA variants reported by Huang et al. (2023), what specific organ malformations were confirmed at autopsy, and were any secondary pathogenic variants found elsewhere in the fetal exomes?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the exact anatomical and molecular autopsy findings of the specific PLAA-positive fetus in Huang et al. will directly resolve whether PLAA caused non-CNS malformations or if the fetus had isolated CNS pathology accompanied by maternal/ultrasound artifacts or a dual molecular lesion.

new_directions.question_text: Do functional null PLAA alleles in cell and animal models impair general non-neuronal organogenesis, or is apoptosis and defective autophagy/endosomal trafficking strictly confined to neuronal and glial populations?
new_directions.rationale: Determining the cellular vulnerability profile of PLAA depletion in non-neuronal tissues (e.g., cardiac, renal, chondrogenic) establishes biological plausibility for whether PLAA can disrupt gross organogenesis outside the nervous system.
